title: Gonur Depe, capital of the Oxus
description: The fortified palace town of the Oxus civilisation, hidden in the Karakum, is the largest Bronze Age city between the Indus and Mesopotamia.

title: Arsaces founds Parthia
description: Arsaces I leads the Parni nomads into Parthia and founds a dynasty that rules Iran for nearly five centuries; its early royal residence stands at Nisa, near Ashgabat.

title: Abu Muslim raises revolt at Merv
description: Abu Muslim hoists the black banners, the start of the movement that overthrows the Umayyads and founds the Abbasid Caliphate.

title: Battle of Dandanaqan
description: The Seljuk Turks rout the army of the Ghaznavid sultan and win an empire stretching from Central Asia into Iran and later Anatolia.

title: Death of Alp Arslan
description: The victor of Manzikert is stabbed by a prisoner while campaigning beyond the Oxus and is buried at Merv.

title: Death of Sultan Sanjar
description: The last great Seljuk sultan dies a broken captive of the Oghuz, and his mausoleum at Merv survives the Mongol sack.

title: Mongols sack Merv
description: Tolui's army butchers the inhabitants of the Khwarazmian Empire's greatest city, by some accounts hundreds of thousands, and Merv never fully recovers.

title: Mongols destroy Gurganj
description: After a siege of months the Mongols take the Khwarazmian capital, drown its people by damming the Amu Darya and enslave the survivors.

title: Battle of Merv
description: Shah Ismail of Persia defeats and kills the Uzbek ruler Muhammad Shaybani, drawing the frontier between Persian and Uzbek lands along the Oxus.

title: Russians found Krasnovodsk
description: A Russian detachment lands on the eastern shore of the Caspian and builds the fort that becomes the base for the conquest of the Turkmen.

title: Teke repulse Russians at Geok Tepe
description: Tekke Turkmen storm out of their desert fortress and rout General Lomakin's assault, a rare Central Asian victory over the Russian army.

title: Fall of Geok Tepe
description: Skobelev's troops blow up the fortress wall and massacre the fleeing defenders, breaking the Tekke and opening the way to Ashgabat and Merv.

title: Ashgabat founded
description: The victors build a fortified camp beside a Tekke village, the seed of Turkmenistan's future capital.

title: Merv submits to Russia
description: The Tekke elders of the Merv oasis swear allegiance to the tsar, extending Russian rule across the whole Turkmen steppe.

title: Panjdeh incident
description: Russian troops scatter an Afghan detachment beside the Kushk river, and Britain and Russia come close to war before agreeing on a border commission.

title: Transcaspian railway reaches Merv
description: The line from Krasnovodsk through Askhabad and Merv turns conquest into settlement and binds the region to Russia.

title: Turkmen SSR formed
description: Soviet national delimitation carves a Turkmen union republic out of the Turkestan, Bukhara and Khorezm territories, the first Turkmen state.

title: Ashgabat earthquake
description: An earthquake destroys Ashgabat at dawn and kills perhaps 110,000 people, including most of the president's family; the news is suppressed abroad.

title: Karakum Canal work begins
description: Digging starts on the canal that will draw a third of the Amu Darya across the Karakum, irrigating cotton and helping to shrink the Aral Sea.

title: Darvaza gas crater
description: A drilling rig punches into a gas cavern and the burning pit known as the Door to Hell is still alight half a century later.

title: Independence
description: After a referendum, Turkmenistan declares independence from the Soviet Union, with Saparmurat Niyazov as its already ruling president.

title: Krasnovodsk becomes Türkmenbaşy
description: The Caspian port is renamed for the president's self-given title, Head of the Turkmen, an early sign of his personality cult.

title: UN recognises Turkmen neutrality
description: The General Assembly backs Niyazov's policy of permanent neutrality, which has kept Turkmenistan out of all alliances since.

title: Ruhnama published
description: The president's book of revisionist history and homespun morals becomes compulsory reading for every Turkmen, from schools to driving tests.

title: Niyazov dies
description: The self-styled Turkmenbashi dies of heart failure after 21 years of absolute rule, and his dentist takes over.

title: Berdimuhamedow elected
description: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow wins a rubber-stamp election and slowly dismantles parts of the Niyazov cult while keeping the autocracy.

title: Gas pipeline to China
description: The presidents of four countries open a pipeline carrying Turkmen gas to China, breaking Russia's old monopoly on Turkmen gas exports.

title: Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games
description: Ashgabat hosts the region's games in a new Olympic complex, a rare moment when the closed country welcomes thousands of foreign athletes.
